name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
summary: Physiotherapy supports medical treatment with joint protection, range of movement, strengthening, aerobic exercise, pacing, hand and foot care and education about flares, adjusting the programme to disease activity.

looksLike: Joint pain, swelling and morning stiffness
Disease activity as reported by the medical team
Hand function, grip and foot posture
redFlags: Hot, very swollen single joint with fever (possible infection)
New neck pain with arm weakness, numbness or gait change (possible cervical instability)
Sudden loss of finger extension (possible tendon rupture)
Unexplained weight loss or persistent fever
firstSteps: Record joint symptoms, morning stiffness, fatigue and hand and foot function.
Ask about disease activity and screen for neck symptoms.
Teach gentle range exercises, pacing and joint protection.
selfCare: Flare plan: relative rest and gentle movement

assess: Joint pain, swelling and morning stiffness
Disease activity as reported by the medical team
Hand function, grip and foot posture
measures: Joint counts as reported by the rheumatology team

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Joint protection and pacing reduce strain, and the team manages medicines.
dose: Range exercises: 5 to 10 repetitions each joint daily.
Aerobic training: 20 to 30 minutes, 3 to 5 days a week at moderate effort in quiet periods.
Resistance training: 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 repetitions, 2 days a week, avoiding flared joints.
Hand exercises: short sessions several times a day.
moveOn: Reduce intensity but keep moving in flares
Review with the rheumatology team for medicines

stages.goal: Neck, hand and foot involvement need particular care.
when: Reduce intensity but keep moving in flares
do: Flare plan: relative rest and gentle movement
dose: Reduce intensity but keep moving in a flare.

manual: Avoid forceful stretching of inflamed joints and the neck
Soft-tissue work for muscle tension; avoid the neck and inflamed joints.
modalities: Heat for stiffness and cold for hot joints if tolerated
Splints for resting or functional support when prescribed
Paraffin wax for hands when suitable
Heat for 10 to 15 minutes for stiffness; cold for hot joints.
Wax baths or splints as appropriate.

mistakes: Ignoring neck symptoms or sudden loss of finger extension.
education: Explain joint protection, pacing and the role of medicines.
Encourage regular physical activity and fatigue management.
escalation: Urgent medical review for suspected joint infection, cervical instability or tendon rupture
Rheumatology review for persistent flares or new joint damage
